planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in average, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Picta is a variegated-leaf sport of Kerria japonica, more compact than the plain green species.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in average, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun. Picta bears leaves edged in a crisp white margin around a gray-green center, providing season-long foliage interest on bright green, arching, bamboo-like canes, in addition to the single golden-yellow flowers that open in mid-spring typical of the species. Its variegated foliage and more compact, refined habit compared with plain green kerria make it useful as a foliage accent in a shaded border even after the spring flower display has finished. Like other kerria it tolerates considerably more shade than most flowering shrubs while still blooming reliably. It suckers moderately to form a colony over time; prune out a portion of the oldest canes at ground level right after flowering each year to keep the planting vigorous and well-shaped, and remove any shoots that revert to solid green to prevent them from overtaking the variegated growth.
